body:

Evidence Recorded: The task's actual deliverable -- a well-evidenced PR-backlog triage doc (merge-base + AST-level function-name diffing against origin/main, real 'gh pr close' proof-citing comments, 34 PRs disposed, 26+10 ranked as still-real) -- is sound methodology and the substantive review turns up no correctness or security defect in it. The problem is the rest of the diff: it permanently commits ~15MB / ~10,400 lines of raw one-off triage scratch into the claude-control repo's history under .triage/ -- full GitHub API JSON payload dumps (vs_funcmatch.json alone is 4240 lines), ad-hoc/oddly-named debug scripts (debug_cc.py, inspect.py, bigtest.txt, test_subproc.py), and several zero-byte error-log placeholders (err1.txt, cc_api_err.txt, vs_api_err.txt). None of this has lasting value beyond the single triage session that produced it -- the curated progress markdown already captures every real finding and citation a future reader needs. Notably the worker itself seems to have recognized this distinction, since it left the much larger .triage/vs_repo/ full clone untracked while still committing everything else in .triage/. Merging this bloats main's permanent history with disposable debug artifacts and sets a bad precedent for future triage-style tasks. No .github/workflows/** paths are touched, so the hard workflow-file rule is not implicated, and there is no schema/auth/payment/secret exposure (spot-checked for tokens/keys -- one grep hit was a false positive, just a PR title mentioning an anthropic-api-key removal task). Issues found: Do not merge .triage/*.json (api1.json, cc_all.json, cc_old.json, cc_overlap.json, cc_classified.json, vs_all.json, vs_old.json, vs_overlap.json, vs_classified.json, vs_funcmatch.json, closed_vs_api.json, closed_vs.json, out1.json) -- these are raw GitHub API dumps with no value once the findings are summarized in the progress doc; drop them from the diff or move to a gitignored scratch path.; Drop ad-hoc/debug scratch files that were clearly one-off aids, not reusable tooling: debug_cc.py, inspect.py, bigtest.txt, test_subproc.py, err1.txt, cc_api_err.txt, vs_api_err.txt, commitmsg.txt, out/ (pr113.diff, pr62_migrate.py, pr72_check.diff, cc_pr_shas.txt, vs_pr_shas.txt, main_progress.md).; If any of the classification scripts (classify.py, funcmatch.py, overlap.py, summarize.py, parse2.py) are meant to be reused for future backlog triage, they belong under a proper tools/ or scripts/ path with a README, not left in a throwaway .triage/ directory alongside disposable data -- otherwise drop them too.; Re-submit with only the curated progress markdown (...triage-and-dispose-the-pre-2026-08-08-st.md) as the diff; the actual PR closures already happened as external gh pr close side effects and are independently verifiable on GitHub, so they don't require this scratch data to be preserved in-repo.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
